_extraction_flags.notes: Hybrid FSO/RF. Sensing target is atmosphere (fog), not physical objects.

reasoning_trace.step_0_visual_inspection: Figure 1: UAV relaying data from FSO Gateway to Ground Users. 'Red arrows' indicate backscattered light unused for comms but used for sensing. Figure 11/14: Performance plots vs Visibility (Fog), indicating weather-dependent sensing.
reasoning_trace.step_1_concept_analysis: System: UAV-aided Mixed FSO-RF Network. Backhaul is FSO (Optical), Access is RF (mmWave). Sensing mechanism: 'Backscattered light' from FSO beam is used to estimate channel gain (fog density) and optimize UAV trajectory. This fits 'Sensing-Assisted Communication' (SAGC).
reasoning_trace.step_2_benchmark_verification: Comm: Max throughput 12x10^8 (1.2 Gbps) for edge users. Sensing: No explicit range/resolution metric; the metric is 'Channel Gain Estimation' used for Trajectory Optimization. SNR thresholds (10 dB vs -10 dB) for sensing feedback are tested.
reasoning_trace.step_3_strategic_critique: Contribution: Novel use of 'backscatter' (normally noise) as a sensing signal to handle adverse weather in FSO UAV links. Gap: Sensing doesn't detect objects/targets, but 'atmospheric condition' (environmental sensing). This is a unique subset of ISAC.

bibliographic.title: Integrated Sensing and Communication for UAV Trajectory Optimization in Mixed FSO-RF Networks in Dynamic Weather Conditions
bibliographic.authors: Muhammad Nafees, Mohammadamin Baniasadi, James R. Hopgood, Majid Safari, John S. Thompson

application.scenario_description: UAV acting as a relay with FSO backhaul, using backscattered light to sense fog density and optimize trajectory.

key_contribution.key_contribution: Proposing an O-ISAC framework where backscattered FSO light guides UAV trajectory optimization via Q-learning to mitigate weather attenuation.
key_contribution.gap_addressed: FSO backhaul reliability in adverse weather (fog) for UAV networks.

receiver.notes: Includes backscatter sensing receiver at the UAV.

waveform.notes: Comm signal itself acts as the sensing probe via backscattering.

channel_wireless.notes: Distance varies with UAV trajectory. Weather: Fog/Haze (Mie scattering).
